headline: LLMs and text mining turn biological text and metadata into structured, queryable…
label: Llm Curation For Genomic Data
summary: External validation of LLM-extracted gene-disease and variant associations is becoming the central test for automated genomic curation at scale.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of large language models and text-mining pipelines to convert unstructured biological text and public repository metadata into structured, queryable resources. The GEO-derived perturbation atlas (6,802 signatures) and GEOMeta's annotation of roughly 600k human bulk RNA-seq samples illustrate automated curation at scale, while PubMind reports a ~1.3M-variant database with an API. What is new is the emphasis on external validation: 74% of LLM-generated phenotype-gene associations matched Ensembl, GWAS Catalog and OMIM, with lower agreement for SNPs, and seven commercial LLMs were benchmarked for extraction from 406 full-text congenital heart disease articles. Retrieval-grounded and multi-agent designs (OncoGenRAG, PlantAI) add auditability, whereas SVlog and KRAKEN address adjacent problems of structural variant logic and provenance-tracked graphs.
